title: Promises to Give & Contribution Receivables
description: Account for unconditional promises to give, contribution receivables, present value, and collectibility.
html:
What Is a Promise to Give?

A promise to give is a donor's written or oral agreement to contribute cash or other assets to an organization in the future.

Unconditional Promise to Give

An unconditional promise to give is generally recognized as contribution revenue when sufficient evidence of the promise exists.

UNCONDITIONAL PROMISE → RECOGNIZE CONTRIBUTION + CONTRIBUTION RECEIVABLE
Example

A donor makes an unconditional promise to contribute $50,000 to an NFP.

The amount will be collected in three months.

Contribution Receivable + $50,000 Contribution Revenue + $50,000

Conditional Promise

A conditional promise generally is not recognized as contribution revenue until the barrier has been substantially overcome.

CONDITIONAL PROMISE → GENERALLY NO CONTRIBUTION RECEIVABLE AND NO CONTRIBUTION REVENUE YET
Example

A donor promises $100,000 if the NFP successfully raises another $100,000 from other donors.

Assume the donor is released from the promise if the matching requirement is not achieved.

Until the barrier has been substantially overcome, the promise generally is not recognized as contribution revenue.

Promise vs. Restriction

An unconditional promise may still contain a donor-imposed restriction.

Example

A donor unconditionally promises $80,000 for a future scholarship program.

The contribution may be recognized, but the donor's purpose or time restriction affects its classification.

UNCONDITIONAL → RECOGNIZE DONOR RESTRICTION → DETERMINE NET ASSET CLASSIFICATION

Promises Due in Future Periods

Unconditional promises expected to be collected in future periods may create a donor-imposed time restriction.

When collection extends beyond one year, measurement may also require consideration of present value.

Present Value

Long-term unconditional promises to give are generally measured using the present value of expected future cash flows, when the effect is material.

FUTURE CONTRIBUTION → DISCOUNT FUTURE CASH FLOWS → PRESENT VALUE
Simplified Example

A donor unconditionally promises $110,000 payable several years in the future.

Assume the present value of the expected future payment is $100,000.

CONTRIBUTION RECEIVABLE $110,000 FACE AMOUNT LESS: DISCOUNT $10,000 NET PRESENT VALUE = $100,000

Collectibility

The organization must also consider whether all recognized promises are expected to be collected.

Estimated uncollectible amounts reduce the net amount expected to be realized.

Example

Contribution receivables total $200,000.

The NFP estimates that $8,000 will not be collected.

$200,000 − $8,000 = $192,000 NET RECEIVABLE

Multi-Year Pledges

A donor may promise payments over several years.

If the promise is unconditional, the NFP generally does not wait for each future cash payment before recognizing the contribution.

CASH COLLECTION DATE ≠ NECESSARILY THE REVENUE RECOGNITION DATE

Example — Three-Year Pledge

A donor makes an unconditional $300,000 pledge payable over three years.

Assume the present value of the expected payments is $275,000.

INITIAL CONTRIBUTION RECOGNIZED = $275,000

The discount related to the future payments changes over time as the collection dates approach.

Conditional vs. Unconditional

Unconditional Promise Generally Recognize When Promise Is Made
Conditional Promise Generally Wait Until Barrier Is Substantially Overcome

CPA Decision Process

STEP 1 IS THE PROMISE CONDITIONAL? YES → GENERALLY WAIT NO → RECOGNIZE STEP 2 IS THERE A DONOR RESTRICTION? STEP 3 IS PAYMENT LONG-TERM? → CONSIDER PRESENT VALUE STEP 4 CONSIDER COLLECTIBILITY

CPA Memory Rule

UNCONDITIONAL PLEDGE = RECEIVABLE NOW CONDITIONAL PLEDGE = GENERALLY WAIT LONG-TERM PLEDGE = THINK PRESENT VALUE

Key Takeaways

  • Unconditional promises to give are generally recognized when made.
  • Conditional promises generally are not recognized until the barrier has been substantially overcome.
  • Donor restrictions affect the classification of recognized contributions.
  • Long-term promises may require present-value measurement.
  • Collectibility affects the net contribution receivable reported.

quiz.prompt: An NFP receives an unconditional promise from a donor to pay $200,000 three years from now. The present value of the expected payment is $175,000. Assuming collectibility is probable, what amount should generally be initially recognized as contribution revenue?
quiz.explanation: Because the promise is unconditional, contribution revenue is generally recognized when the promise is made. For a material long-term promise, the contribution is initially measured using present value, which is $175,000.
